expectations.text: Enhanced prompt is delivered in a clearly marked copy-paste block, separate from commentary
expectations.evidence: The prompt is introduced with 'ready to paste into an AI coding assistant' and delimited by horizontal rules ('---') on both sides, with commentary in a separate 'Notes on what I changed and why' section. Marginal: it is markdown between separators, not a fenced code block, so the copy boundary is less crisp than a code fence.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt states the intent/goal (raise conversion, Black Friday deadline), not just the task
expectations.evidence: Prompt block: 'We need the checkout page fixed and improved before Black Friday, with the primary business goal of increasing checkout conversion rate.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt names the specific known bug (coupon field crashes on empty input)
expectations.evidence: Prompt block: 'Critical: coupon field crashes on empty input. Reproduce and fix the crash that occurs when the coupon code field is submitted (or applied) while empty.'

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt defines success criteria or scope boundaries (what 'better' means, what's out of scope)
expectations.evidence: 'Constraints & deliverables' section: 'Don't redesign the visual brand... Don't change pricing, tax, or payment-provider logic beyond what's needed... Summarize at the end: root cause of the coupon crash, every bug found and fixed...'

expectations.text: Response includes change notes explaining what changed and why (not just the rewritten prompt)
expectations.evidence: '## Notes on what I changed and why' section with five bullets, e.g. 'Split "better" into two concrete workstreams — bug fixes and conversion improvements — and ordered them'.

expectations.text: Enhanced prompt does not name any specific AI model or vendor
expectations.evidence: The enhanced prompt block contains no AI model or vendor names; it references only React, the app, and generic 'the assistant'.

claims.claim: The likely root causes listed for the coupon crash (e.g. '.trim() on undefined') are speculative since no codebase was inspected
claims.evidence: The response asserts 'Likely causes to check: calling .trim()/.toUpperCase() on undefined/null...' without access to the code; framed as hypotheses to check, so acceptable, but unverifiable.

claims.claim: Part 2 conversion tactics have 'proven impact on checkout conversion'
claims.evidence: The prompt says 'Prioritize changes with proven impact on checkout conversion' — the tactics listed are conventional best practices but no evidence is cited; claim is plausible but unverified.

suggestions.assertion: Enhanced prompt is delivered in a clearly marked copy-paste block, separate from commentary
suggestions.reason: This run passes with '---' separators rather than a fenced code block; if the skill specifically requires a fenced/code-block delivery, tighten the assertion to 'fenced code block' so the two formats are distinguished.

eval_feedback.overall: Both runs pass all assertions; the eval does not currently separate skill from baseline behavior.
